summary: The bill repeals the District of Columbia's Comprehensive Policing and Justice Reform Amendment Act of 2022 except for its subtitles on use-of-force reporting and body-worn cameras, restoring prior law as if the 2022 Act had not been enacted.

scores.thoughts: The bill repeals a District of Columbia policing and justice reform law but contains no provisions that authorize, appropriate, or alter any federal or local spending levels. It is silent on budgets, funding streams, or expenditures.
No tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue provisions appear in the bill text.
The legislation addresses only criminal-justice statutes in the District of Columbia and has no bearing on healthcare delivery, insurance, or public-health programs.

Although the repealed 2022 DC act may have contained ancillary provisions touching firearms, the bill itself makes no reference to gun regulations, permitting, or enforcement and therefore does not engage the topic.
No immigration, border, or visa provisions are present.
The bill is confined to policing and criminal-justice statutes and does not address reproductive-health policy.
No defense-authorization or military-spending language exists.
The measure contains no environmental, regulatory, or energy provisions.
Nothing in the bill alters eligibility, funding, or administration of welfare, nutrition, or other safety-net programs.
No education, school-choice, or federal-education-program provisions are included.
The bill does not amend controlled-substance statutes or enforcement priorities.

The bill repeals the bulk of the District of Columbia’s 2022 Comprehensive Policing and Justice Reform Amendment Act, restoring prior statutory language. That 2022 act was a package of police-accountability and sentencing reforms; its repeal therefore shifts DC policy away from reform-oriented measures and toward the pre-existing, more enforcement-oriented framework. This constitutes a direct and substantial engagement with criminal-justice policy.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions appear.
The bill neither authorizes new spending nor enacts deficit-reduction measures.
No civil-rights or anti-discrimination provisions related to sexual orientation or gender identity are present.
The legislation does not address foreign assistance.
No election-administration or voting-access provisions exist.
The bill contains no data-privacy, surveillance, or technology-regulation language.
No labor, collective-bargaining, or workplace-regulation provisions are included.
The bill does not address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination balances.
